explanation: Summers calls Goichman circuit precedent directly on the due process issue, but Goichman is a full signed, reasoned Tenth Circuit opinion printed in F.2d; it is published, so limb 1 fails.

Rivera holds the argument foreclosed by Slaughter and says the court is bound by it, but Slaughter at 238 F.3d 580 is a published per curiam on rehearing (the earlier unpublished opinion is only an attachment); limb 1 fails.

Colon is a published Illinois Supreme Court opinion (the Rule 23 order was the appellate decision it reviewed). Williams only quotes Colon's general stare decisis principles; the controlling precedent followed is Nicholls. Limbs 1 and 2 fail.

In re S.H. is a published Illinois Appellate opinion (the Rule 23 order was Heiman's earlier criminal appeal). The citing court distinguished S.H. and declined to follow the trial court's reliance on it. Limbs 1 and 2 fail.

Malone says it is bound by McNeal, but cites it as 735 F.3d 1263 and calls it a 'prior published decision'; the originally unpublished opinion had been ordered published (per the citation given), so limb 1 fails.
The court applies Akau as 'our precedent' on injury-in-fact standing, but Akau is a signed, reasoned Hawaii Supreme Court opinion printed in Hawaii Reports; it is published, so limb 1 fails.

Berger states a rule 'by which we are bound' quoting Turner v. Noto, a reasoned opinion sharing page 151 So.2d 303; it never cites the Wood v. Wolfe per curiam affirmance. Wrong cited decision matched; limb 1 fails for the case actually relied on.
